question: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible for anaphylaxis?
explanation: Anaphylaxis is an immediate Type I IgE-mediated reaction involving mast cells and basophils. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h1)

question: What happens when mast cells degranulate during an allergic reaction?

options.A: Inflammatory mediators are released into tissues
options.B: Antibodies stop the immune system response
options.C: Red blood cells multiply rapidly in vessels
options.D: Platelets clot to close open blood vessels

explanation: Degranulation releases stored chemicals like histamine, which causes sudden widespread blood vessel widening and swelling. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which group of medications is a common cause of severe anaphylaxis?
explanation: Antibiotics such as penicillin are well-known triggers for severe allergic drug reactions. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h2)

question: Why do insect stings often cause quick, body-wide reactions in sensitive people?

options.A: Sting sites always develop severe local bacterial infections
options.B: Insect toxins permanently destroy bone marrow cells
options.C: Venom enters the bloodstream directly and spreads
options.D: Venom triggers an immediate drop in body temperature

explanation: When venom is injected directly into tissues or vessels, allergens quickly reach mast cells throughout the body. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which skin change is most typical of an acute allergic reaction?
explanation: Hives and skin flushing happen because histamine causes blood vessels to widen and leak fluid into the skin layers. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h3)

question: A patient having an allergic reaction develops wheezing and throat tightness. What causes this?
explanation: Immune chemicals make airway muscles tighten and mucosal tissues swell, which blocks normal breathing. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary assessment framework to use first for a patient in acute anaphylaxis?
explanation: The ABC approach helps nurses quickly spot and manage life-threatening breathing and circulation problems. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h4)

question: A patient develops noisy breathing and low blood pressure shortly after receiving medication. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Offer the patient a glass of cold oral water
options.B: Leave the bedside to find the attending physician
options.C: Call for emergency assistance and prepare epinephrine
options.D: Document the exact vital signs in the patient chart

explanation: Noisy breathing and low blood pressure point to a life-threatening emergency that needs immediate help and fast medication. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the main medication used to treat acute anaphylaxis?
explanation: Epinephrine works quickly to reverse airway tightening and low blood pressure. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why is epinephrine injected into the thigh muscle rather than the arm?

options.A: Subcutaneous tissue in the arm delays drug breakdown entirely
options.B: Absorption is faster and more reliable from the vastus lateralis
options.C: Thigh injections cause significantly less local pain for adults
options.D: The deltoid muscle contains too many nerves and blood vessels

explanation: The large thigh muscle has a rich blood supply, which helps the medication enter the bloodstream quickly. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h5)

question: What is a biphasic anaphylactic reaction?

options.A: An allergic response caused by two different drugs at once
options.B: A return of symptoms without re-exposure to the trigger
options.C: A mild skin reaction that turns into a fever days later
options.D: An infection developing after a severe insect sting site

explanation: A biphasic reaction happens when allergic symptoms return hours after the first episode seemed to completely clear up. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h6)

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between a simple fainting spell and anaphylaxis?

options.A: Vasovagal attacks cause severe swelling of the upper airway
options.B: Vasovagal episodes usually feature bradycardia instead of tachycardia
options.C: Vasovagal reactions respond rapidly to intramuscular epinephrine
options.D: Vasovagal syncope always includes widespread itchy hives

explanation: Fainting or vasovagal episodes usually slow the heart rate down, whereas anaphylaxis typically speeds the heart up while dropping blood pressure. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h6)

question: What device should patients with a history of severe allergies carry at all times?
explanation: Carrying an epinephrine autoinjector allows quick self-treatment if the person accidentally touches or eats their allergen. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why is it important for someone prone to severe allergies to wear a medical alert bracelet?

options.A: It automatically releases emergency medication when skin temperature rises
options.B: It alerts local food vendors to keep ingredients completely allergen-free
options.C: It prevents the immune system from producing high levels of IgE
options.D: It provides immediate health details if the patient becomes unresponsive

explanation: Medical alert tags give healthcare workers vital allergy information fast if the patient is unable to speak. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h7)
